name: Streaming Embrace The Sec 0Bd123A5C0
text: Embrace the SEC presents the following source proposition: Securities law traditionally only permits corporations that have registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and completed an initial public offering (IPO) to sell equity to the general public—often a long, expensive process. This proposition is pertinent to Kaal's source-bound claim that Overstock.com issued the first SEC registered digital securities using blockchain technology, and because the issuer was a public company conducting a shelf registration, the offering functions as a working model of blockchain benefits and as a map of the U.S. regulatory gaps. The proposed response is an extension: the relationship should remain limited to the retrieved source proposition and the mapped Kaal claim unless fuller source review supports a broader conclusion.
